messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: Elevated 5xx rate and connection failures for inference-api.redwood-prod in us-east-1 (start=1863002466). Alert: high-error-rate, source=elb, metric=HTTP_5XX, severity=high. /ops oncall
oncall-alex: got the page, I'll look. Any customer-visible errors?
support-alyssa: seeing spikes in 502/504 from multiple customers in us-east. Many requests time out after 10s. Ticket volume increasing.
sre-michael: copying logs — ELB reports target health flapping in us-east-1a and us-east-1c, targets draining then re-registering. Backend EC2s are up but returning TCP RSTs intermittently.
eng-ops-jess: can someone check if there's a Route53 failover or healthcheck that's flipping? We recently pushed a small change to the weighted routing in us-east for blue/green.
netops-sam: looking at Route53 — health checks for inference-api-us-east are showing 30% failures from multiple regions starting ~1863002400. No config changes in the last 24h on our side.
sre-michael: ELB logs attached (snippet):
```
Time: 2024-11-29T12:01:23Z client: 10.10.10.5:34567 backend: 10.0.12.34:443 elb_status:502 backend_status:0 "GET /v1/generate"
Time: 2024-11-29T12:02:10Z client: 10.10.10.6:34568 backend: 10.0.12.36:443 elb_status:504 backend_status:0 "POST /v1/chat"
```
sre-michael: notice backend_status 0 — means connection failed before backend could respond. Could be ENI or AZ network fabric.
eng-ops-jess: can we fail traffic to another region quickly? Is cross-region routing warmed?
oncall-alex: plan: 1) lower Route53 TTL to 30s, 2) shift weight from us-east pool to us-west-2 fallback, 3) open support case with AWS about ELB/ENI flaps, 4) keep customers informed.
support-alyssa: preparing status message for customers: short blurb + estimated mitigation time 15-30m.
pm-rita: add severity note: potential partial region outage for inference API affecting ~20% of traffic for a subset of customers. Prioritize high-commit customers.
netops-sam: lowering Route53 global TTL now (change propagated). Command:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch file://lower-ttl.json
# lower A/alias TTL to 30
```
netops-sam: initiating weighted shift to move 70% traffic off us-east to us-west-2 (manual weight change).
eng-ops-jess: confirm blue/green weights? ensure session affinity not causing single-customer storms.
sre-michael: rolling a fast kill switch on ELB target group health check threshold — increase unhealthy threshold to avoid thrashing while we fail traffic out. Command applied to target-group tg-abc123.
oncall-alex: opened AWS support case (case 1234567890) requesting investigation into ELB control plane and AZ network fabric in us-east-1. AWS Support assigned Level 2.
aws-support-bot: Case 1234567890: We are seeing increased ELB control plane error rates in us-east-1 regions 1a/1c, AWS networking team investigating. We'll update in 15 minutes.
sre-michael: immediate mitigation metrics: error rate dropped 40% after shifting 70% traffic, latency improved for routed-to region. Some customers with geolocation pins still see issues.
eng-ops-jess: executing edge rule to prefer nearest healthy region: updating CloudFront origin failover list for inference-api -> added us-west-2 primary for fallback.
support-alyssa: status update posted to status.redwood.ai: "We are investigating partial regional degradation in us-east-1 impacting API calls. Traffic is being shifted to healthy regions; mitigation in progress."
pm-rita: coordinate with sales for top-10 customers — notify account leads.
sre-michael: handoff: I'm going offline for 20m to join AWS call; handing to eng-ops-jess to continue mitigation. @eng-ops-jess can you own until I return? :handshake:
eng-ops-jess: taking over. continuing to monitor. Next actions: monitor ELB target registration, rollback any recent route53 automated rollouts, prepare for full cutover if flaps continue.
eng-ops-jess: observation — some EBS-backed instances in us-east show transient attach/detach activity (could be symptomatic of control plane problems). I'm suspending any scaling in us-east to avoid further state churn.
netops-sam: AWS update: "We have observed API throttling for EC2/ELB control plane in us-east-1 affecting target registration and ENI updates. Working on mitigation."
support-alyssa: customers with active sessions — recommend retries and sticky session fallback where possible. Sending outbound email to impacted customers with mitigation steps.
eng-ops-jess: running smoke test against fallback region: OK for typical request patterns. Will gradually increase weight if stable.
oncall-alex: status check — errors down 65% overall, latency stable for routed traffic, AWS investigating. Suspect regional control plane partial outage affecting ELB/ENI state.
sre-michael: returning — any new findings?
eng-ops-jess: still seeing intermittent target flaps for a small subset. AWS suggests their engineers are applying mitigations; they expect control plane API call rates to normalize over next 30-60m.
pm-rita: customer impact summary for postmortem: start=1863002400, affected region=us-east-1, components=ELB target registration, ENI/EC2 control plane, Route53 health checks. Impact: increased 5xx for ~20% of traffic, partial session loss for sessions pinned to affected AZs.
support-alyssa: collecting impacted customer list and TTL of caches for CDNs — prepping targeted communications.
eng-ops-jess: once AWS confirms control plane stable, we'll slowly reweight traffic back to normal and raise TTLs back to standard.
oncall-alex: handoff to night oncall @sre-michael at 1863003300 — leaving notes in pagerduty and handoff channel. If AWS resolves fully, mark incident resolved; otherwise escalate to engineering lead.
sre-michael: acknowledged. final checks before handoff: 1) CloudWatch error rate trending down, 2) Route53 TTL lowered and weight change reversible, 3) open AWS case and contact list attached.
incident-bot: Incident incident-1863002468: status=mitigated; assigned_to=sre-michael; severity=high; start_ts=1863002466; update_ts=1863003310.
